articles.title: Home Assistant adjusts Zonneplan battery limits and reserves
articles.dek: Power limits and trading thresholds respect the battery’s selected operating mode.
body: Home Assistant adds controls for a Zonneplan home battery’s maximum charging and discharging power, backup energy reserve and minimum price difference for day-ahead trading. Each setting follows the battery’s reported capabilities, and the backup-reserve control is disabled by default.

Power limits apply in home-optimization mode, while the trading threshold applies in arbitrage mode. Each edit first checks the battery’s current mode, preventing a settings change from silently switching it. Erwin Douna adds the controls; he notes that the controls have not been tested against a real battery.

pullRequests.title: Add Zonneplan battery number entities

articles.title: Matter.js tightens the identity checks used when pairing devices
articles.dek: Controllers reject untrusted certification signatures and malformed device certificates under the default policy.
body: Matter.js strengthens the checks a controller uses to decide whether a device’s identity and certification evidence can be trusted during pairing. Its default policy refuses certification declarations from unknown signers and certificates that violate the required device profile.

Ingo Fischer adds built-in trusted signing keys so a controller can check known certification signatures without an internet connection. A signing certificate fetched from the online ledger must still prove that the Connectivity Standards Alliance issued it.

Applications built on the library can supply their own policy for handling failed checks. These changes concern the controller library; they do not establish availability in a particular Home Assistant release.

pullRequests.title: fix(protocol): validate Certification Declarations and trust CD signers as CHIP does
fix(protocol): enforce the DAC and PAI certificate profile in device attestation

articles.title: Sendspin guides Windows setup to the chosen speaker
articles.dek: The command-line player removes a missing-runtime obstacle and gives new installations an output menu.
body: Sendspin’s C++ command-line player bundles the runtime needed to start on a Windows computer without a separate Visual C++ installation. Its setup script also asks for a player name and offers a short list of audio outputs, with the system default as the initial choice.

The selected speaker is saved by name and audio interface rather than a device number that can change when a monitor, Bluetooth device or headset comes and goes. Existing configured names and outputs stay in place during upgrades.
A new uninstaller removes the player, its startup task and firewall rule. Saved configuration and pairings remain unless the owner chooses to remove them too.

pullRequests.title: Link the static CRT so the Windows zip runs on a clean install
Let a PortAudio device name carry its host API
Ask for a name and an output on Windows, and add an uninstaller

articles.title: ESPHome smooths the steps in very dim lights
articles.dek: An optional ESP32 setting adds finer brightness levels without lowering the light’s switching frequency.
body: ESPHome adds finer low-brightness control for lights driven by an ESP32’s LED controller. Optional hardware dithering spreads fractional brightness levels across pulses, reducing the visible jumps that gamma correction can leave near the bottom of a fade.

Jakub Sztandera makes his first contribution to ESPHome with the addition. It stays off by default and was checked on ESP32-C3 hardware; other supported ESP32 variants were checked against their register layouts and compiled. Very low switching frequencies and brightness can still introduce visible flicker.

pullRequests.title: [ledc] Add hardware duty dithering for supported ESP32 variants
[ledc] Document hardware duty dithering

articles.title: Music Assistant uses Jellyfin’s track and album volume levels
articles.dek: Stored loudness information helps keep a self-hosted music collection at a consistent listening level.
body: Music Assistant reads Jellyfin’s stored loudness information to keep music from a self-hosted library at a consistent listening level. Track measurements are supported, with album measurements available from Jellyfin 12.1.

Florin Popescu makes his first contribution to Music Assistant’s server with the addition. Reading the original values preserves the precision of track measurements and retains album measurements that the existing helper library discarded.

pullRequests.title: Jellyfin replaygain tags

articles.title: Home Assistant can arm Homematic with known exceptions
articles.dek: The explicit override leaves the blocking windows or unreachable devices unmonitored.
body: Home Assistant adds an Arm anyway action for Homematic IP Cloud alarms after an ordinary arm command is refused. It allows arming with the known blocking devices excluded, such as an open window or an unreachable sensor; those entry points remain unmonitored.

The action checks again before proceeding and refuses if more sensors are blocking than in the refusal already shown to the owner. This adds an explicit override to the blocked-arming status covered earlier this week.

pullRequests.title: Add an arm anyway action to HomematicIP Cloud

articles.title: Music Assistant’s Squeezebox library restores JiveLite track progress
articles.dek: Elapsed and remaining time advance instead of leaving the player’s screen at the start of a song.
body: Music Assistant’s Squeezebox connection library corrects the status messages that left JiveLite screens showing a stationary progress bar with no elapsed or remaining time. The player had interpreted a field containing zero as a signal that playback was still waiting to begin.

The correction reports that waiting state only while audio is buffering and removes an empty audio-quality label above the bar. In the contributor’s piCorePlayer comparison, the repaired screen showed 1:31 elapsed where the original remained at the start.

media.caption: The contributor’s piCorePlayer screenshot after the status-message correction.

articles.title: Home Assistant checks whether a Škoda is closed and locked
articles.dek: Vehicle status adds doors, windows, lights and openings alongside the parking location.
body: Home Assistant adds readings for whether a Škoda is locked and whether its doors, windows, boot or bonnet are open. It also reports the lights and, when fitted, the sunroof using the vehicle status already fetched by the integration.

These are readings, not remote locking controls. Unknown vehicle values stay unknown, and charging-plug status is outside this addition. Philipp Ballhausen extends the parking-location work covered yesterday with information about how the car was left.

articles.title: ESPHome lets makers shape LD6004 detection areas
articles.dek: Area selection, height limits and an apply button turn the radar’s position readings into configurable zones.
body: ESPHome adds controls for configuring detection areas on the Hi-Link LD6004 radar. Makers can select an area, change its coordinates and apply the settings, alongside height limits and the time for which presence is held.

Yesterday’s addition exposed presence and target positions; this step lets makers define the spaces the radar watches. Numeric settings that the module refuses or fails to receive are no longer displayed as though they succeeded.

articles.title: ESPHome’s connection library notices a quick power cycle sooner
articles.dek: A fresh device announcement can end the wait on a connection left stale by a brief outage.
body: ESPHome’s connection library detects devices that return from a quick power cut while their old connection still looks active. It probes again when the restarted device announces itself, even if an earlier keepalive request is still awaiting an answer.

The contributor describes a reconnect wait falling from up to 20 seconds to roughly one second after the device returns to the network. Probing becomes the default for applications sharing network discovery, while the command-line log connection keeps its existing default.

articles.title: Home Assistant repairs Android lights stuck in the off state
articles.dek: Dimmable Device Controls keep responding after a light is switched off.
body: Home Assistant’s Android app repairs a failure that could leave a dimmable light’s Device Control repeatedly sending an off command when tapped. After an on-and-off cycle, Android could retain the old touch handling instead of turning the light back on.
The control keeps the same type of brightness-capable interface in both states, preventing that stale handling. Wear OS continues to hide its brightness slider while the light is off.

articles.title: ESPHome controls brushless motors through M5Stack’s driver
articles.dek: Makers can set a target speed, reverse direction and read the motor’s actual rotation rate.
body: ESPHome adds support for the M5Stack M5Unit-BLDC brushless motor driver. Makers can choose direct power control or a target rotation speed, change direction, and read the actual speed and motor status.

Ludovic BOUÉ verified the driver with an M5Stack AtomS3 and a real motor unit. Direction changes briefly stop the drive before restoring it, and the target-speed mode uses the driver’s own feedback control.

articles.title: ESPHome adds infrared controls for Panasonic heat pumps
articles.dek: Compatible models gain climate settings and frost protection while optionally following their original remote.
body: ESPHome adds infrared climate controls for Panasonic air conditioners and heat pumps using the 216-bit Panasonic protocol. The component sends a complete settings frame and, with an infrared receiver, follows changes from the physical remote.

Mikkel Jeppesen adds heating, cooling, drying, fan and automatic modes, plus fixed vertical vane positions. The Away preset sends 10°C frost protection and recognizes an 8°C request from the original remote. Command frames matched 17 recordings from a real remote; Quiet, Powerful and nanoe-G toggle commands remain excluded.

articles.title: ESPHome makes energy-meter alarm limits configurable
articles.dek: ATM90E32 setups can choose voltage, current and frequency thresholds and avoid a false overvoltage warning.
body: ESPHome lets ATM90E32 energy-meter builders set the voltage sag, overvoltage, overcurrent and frequency limits behind their status readings. It also corrects a default limit that could wrap around and report overvoltage at an ordinary 120 volts on boards with a low voltage gain.

The limits follow calibration changes instead of staying tied to the previous gain. Related calibration handling verifies the chip’s settings before saving them and restores the previous values if saving fails.

articles.title: Home Assistant totals Hanna’s chemical dosing
articles.dek: Long-term statistics count each dosing cycle, with a repair for existing sensor histories.
body: Home Assistant changes Hanna’s acid/base and chlorine dosing readings so long-term statistics add up the volume delivered across dosing cycles. The device’s counter rises during a cycle and returns to zero afterward, so treating it as a momentary measurement did not describe its behaviour correctly.

The readings are renamed from flow rate to injection volume, while existing entity identifiers stay unchanged. Existing installations receive a statistics repair because the way these two readings are counted changes.
